target.title: fix(dashboard): tunnel superseded Bay terminal cards to live retry
target.body:
## Summary

- Prioritize Bay terminal-buffer and recently-washed item keys in the bounded exact-review queue projection.
- Let the existing Bay transition logic see a pending replacement review and suppress the superseded terminal failure/cancellation card.
- Preserve the public 24-item sample bound and normal round-robin lane fill.

## Problem

Exact-review workflow attempts that end in an expected held/superseded state can appear in Bay's terminal buffer while a newer durable-queue retry is pending. The public queue projection previously sampled independently, so it could omit that replacement item; Bay then had no active row to tunnel back into the earlier lane.

## Implementation

The status worker passes bounded, validated Bay item keys to the exact-review queue stats endpoint. The queue resolves those keys against live items before applying its public sample cap, then backfills the remaining slots round-robin. Stale terminal records cannot consume priority slots before a matching live retry is found.

## Validation

- `pnpm exec node --test test/dashboard-worker.test.ts` (144 passing)
- `pnpm run build:dashboard`
- `pnpm run lint:dashboard`
- `pnpm run check:dashboard-queue-boundary`
- `git diff --check`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check dashboard/exact-review-queue.ts dashboard/worker.ts test/dashboard-worker.test.ts`

The added regression coverage verifies a matching retry after stale Bay cards and confirms that priority rows still backfill to the 24-item public sample cap.

## Review closeout

- `codex review --uncommitted`: clean after addressing priority matching and sample-backfill findings.
- `codex review --base origin/main`: clean; no accepted/actionable findings.

## Risks / rollout

Only the dashboard's bounded queue projection ordering changes; queue state, workflow dispatch, and publication behavior are untouched. Query keys are validated, deduplicated, and capped at 40 before reaching the durable object.

target.title: fix: honor elevated maintainer roles in bulk-filer policy
target.body:
## Summary

Prevent the bulk-filer policy from incorrectly labelling an organisation maintainer when GitHub's App-token issue payload redacts their `author_association` as `CONTRIBUTOR`.

## Problem

After [#657](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/657) moved bulk-filer mutation into the write-capable publisher, live evidence for [openclaw/openclaw#109684](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/109684) showed a discrepancy:

- the persisted/App-visible item state and an unauthenticated public-equivalent REST response said `CONTRIBUTOR`;
- an authenticated maintainer API response said `MEMBER`;
- the repository collaborator-permission API reported the author as `admin`.

That made a legitimate high-volume maintainer issue eligible for `clawsweeper:bulk-filed`. A normal contributor ([openclaw/openclaw#109911](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/109911)) returned `read` and must remain eligible. Historical labels were corrected manually; this PR is preventative only.

## Implementation

- Add a lazy, cached collaborator-permission fallback for only bulk-filer candidate **issues** whose author association is not already owner/member.
- Exempt only `admin` and `maintain`; ordinary `write` collaborators remain within the policy.
- Keep the publisher as the sole label mutator and remove a stale ClawSweeper-owned bulk label when the elevated role is detected.
- Persist the bulk-filer state from the last full review. When the exemption makes a cached, bulk-suppressed review stale, force exactly one new full review rather than reusing that cache entry.
- Fail closed on a permission lookup failure, preserving the existing policy rather than broadening the exemption.

## Validation

```text
pnpm run build
node --test test/bulk-filer-policy.test.ts test/apply-label-sync.test.ts
pnpm run lint:src
pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/clawsweeper.ts test/bulk-filer-policy.test.ts test/apply-label-sync.test.ts
git diff --check
```

All passed: 32 focused tests. The integration proof exercises the write-side publisher removing a stale label for an App-redacted `maintain` role and verifies it does not create a label. Unit proof covers `admin`, `maintain`, and ordinary `write`.

Linux local-container Crabbox proof also passed on lease `cbx_68e92e0efbf3` (`mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.60.0-noble`): `pnpm run build` and all 11 `test/local-range-review.test.ts` tests.

Codex review closeout:

- `codex review --uncommitted` — clean; accepted and corrected the cache-transition, legacy-report, local-only, and issue-only edge cases during the review loop.
- `codex review --base origin/main` — clean: no actionable correctness issues identified.

## Evidence

- [#109684 worker](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29609443086) and [publisher](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29609574146)
- [#109911 worker](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29609548303) and [publisher](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29609706238)
- Related: [#657](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/657)

## Risk / rollout

The additional API read is lazy, cached per author, issue-only, and limited to already eligible bulk-filer candidates. It does not change workflow scopes, gates, or normal contributor treatment. No historical GitHub state is changed by this PR.

target.title: feat(dashboard): improve OpenClaw Bay telemetry
target.body:
## Summary

Refines the experimental **OpenClaw Bay** demo so its new operational cues are legible and discoverable without turning the beach into a second Overview page.

- adds compact 6-hour / 24-hour / 7-day controls to the Bay telemetry cards;
- gives both mini charts labelled vertical scales and exact point values on hover;
- turns the tiny `+N queued IDs not shown` note into a readable, keyboard-accessible details drawer;
- adds small, accessible lane-help affordances describing what each beach grouping represents; and
- refreshes the deterministic browser evidence to exercise the new controls and disclosure behaviour.

## Problem

The initial compact telemetry presentation had no numeric scale and was fixed to the six-hour view. Queue overflow also looked like a small, non-interactive footnote, while the lane groupings were not self-explanatory to someone encountering the visual view for the first time.

## Implementation

The Bay remains a lightweight presentation of existing dashboard state:

- Range selection uses the established same-origin `/api/health-history?range=` endpoint and retains each selected range in a 60-second in-page cache.
- Axis labels adapt to the selected data and each SVG point has an exact accessible hover title.
- The queue drawer lists every known reference in the *bounded public projection*. When an aggregate count contains references outside that sample, it explicitly says so rather than fetching, guessing, or inventing IDs.
- Lane-help text uses native disclosure semantics, keyboard focus, and the existing stage names.

## API / data impact

This UI adds **no direct browser-to-GitHub API calls** and no mutations. It uses only the existing dashboard `/api/status` and cache-backed `/api/health-history` endpoints. The selected range is cached in the page for 60 seconds, so changing between a previously loaded range does not re-fetch it. This does not add a new GitHub API scan or a parallel telemetry source.

## Validation

- `node --test test/dashboard-worker.test.ts test/exact-review-health.test.ts` — **154 passed, 0 failed**
- `pnpm run lint:dashboard` — passed
- `pnpm run build:dashboard` — passed
- `node --check docs/proof/openclaw-bay/run-proof.mjs` — passed
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check dashboard/bay-page.ts test/dashboard-worker.test.ts docs/proof/openclaw-bay/run-proof.mjs` — passed
- `git diff --check` — clean
- Deterministic Playwright/Crabbox proof — **39 assertions, 21 evidence frames, 0 direct GitHub API requests, 0 mutations**
- `pnpm run review -- --local-range --target-repo openclaw/clawsweeper --base origin/main` — clean local ClawSweeper review: no findings or rank-up work; security cleared; browser proof sufficient.
- `codex review --uncommitted` — clean after accepted P2 fixes for dense terminal overflow and proof-artifact provenance.
- `codex review --base origin/main` — final clean review: no actionable correctness issues.

The repository-wide `pnpm run format:check` remains baseline-noisy on unrelated existing files, so this PR verifies formatting only across its touched source/test/proof-runner files.

## Visual proof

The tracked storyboard covers range switching, labelled chart axes, hover values, queue disclosure, lane help, the existing search/tide interactions, and portrait layout.

![OpenClaw Bay deterministic proof storyboard](docs/proof/openclaw-bay/playwright-proof-storyboard.jpg)

Proof provenance: source `36525da82e489251ecf37454489a0e997a0c0604`; Crabbox local-container lease `cbx_7c27d4e0df99` (`jade-hermit`). The checked-in [`proof-summary.json`](docs/proof/openclaw-bay/proof-summary.json) records the fixture hashes, all assertions, and network/mutation counts.

## Risks / rollout

- The mini telemetry is deliberately advisory: cached history can be incomplete or stale, which the cards continue to label rather than converting to a false zero.
- Hidden aggregate queue references intentionally remain hidden; Bay neither broadens public data nor performs a follow-up fetch to enumerate them.
- This changes only the existing unlisted experimental Bay route. No deployment/configuration, workflow, permission, dependency, or changelog change is included.

Related: Bay’s compact telemetry is a presentation of the health-history and exact-review data already surfaced on Overview.

target.title: fix(terminal): fork the Resize auth check onto the per-subscription queue
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Terminal frames from a client are processed on a single shared per-connection `queue` (all
multiplexed sessions on that WebSocket serialize through it). The `Resize` handler `await`ed
`subscription.canInput()` — an authorization **DB round-trip** — **inline on that shared queue**. So
while one session's resize auth check was in flight, every other session's `Input` / `Subscribe` /
`Stop` / `Ping` frame was head-of-line-blocked behind it.

The `Input` path already avoids exactly this: it forks its own `canInput()` check onto a
per-subscription queue and returns from the shared queue immediately. `Resize` did not.

## The change

Fork the `canInput()` check and the resize work onto `subscription.inputQueue` (the same
per-subscription queue `Input` uses), so the shared connection queue returns immediately. The forked
work re-checks subscription identity before touching the upstream (the same stale-subscription guard
the `Input` path uses).

## Real-behaviour proof (before → after)

The real `TerminalHub`: subscribe, send a `Resize` whose `canInput()` stays pending, then a `Ping`:

```
BASE (origin/main — Resize awaits canInput() inline on the shared queue)
  Ping behind a slow Resize -> pongs before the resize auth resolves = 0   => HEAD-OF-LINE BLOCKED

HEAD (this PR — Resize forked onto the per-subscription queue)
  Ping behind a slow Resize -> pongs before the resize auth resolves = 1   => NOT BLOCKED
```

Reproducible transcript: https://gist.github.com/anagnorisis2peripeteia/25bc9d5c49061e65c33dc4cf27985298

A live WebSocket cannot inject latency into the real authorization DB check, so this deterministic
real-`TerminalHub` reproduction is the strongest feasible proof for a head-of-line *stall*.

## Testing

`pnpm check`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm exec wrangler deploy --dry-run`, `pnpm test` all green.
`tests/terminal-hub.test.ts` adds: a slow Resize does not block a following Ping (the fix); and an
authorized Resize applies the new size and notifies both client and upstream. Mutation of the changed
range scores 76%. A concurrency lint of the diff is clean.

Related: FINDING 4 of #88.
